title: Analyzing post-2000 groundwater level and rainfall changes in Rajasthan, India, using well observations and GRACE data

anchor_context.seed_role: task seed exclusion; not included as a reference direction
anchor_context.extraction_basis: Ex-ante research design reconstructed from independently selected full-text evidence; empirical results are excluded from idea fields.

idea.research_question: How do precipitation variability and GRACE terrestrial water-storage anomalies jointly explain groundwater-level change in semi-arid basins?
idea.hypothesis: Rainfall controls recharge while GRACE captures basin-scale storage response; combining both with well observations should separate climatic recharge from persistent depletion.
idea.mechanism: Monthly precipitation and GRACE anomalies are aligned with well records, then trend, correlation and lag analyses test recharge response and storage decline.
idea.analytical_approach: Multi-source groundwater trend analysis, lagged correlation and storage-response attribution
idea.expected_contribution: A reproducible benchmark for testing whether a proposed idea preserves all required data roles and adds auxiliary data only for a distinct mechanism, validation or refinement purpose.
idea.falsification_condition: The idea fails if it drops a required role, cannot align the required inputs, or does not improve explanatory, predictive or validation performance over the appropriate single-source baseline.
